sections.html:
Chesterfield is a western suburb of St. Louis in St. Louis County, about 25 miles from downtown. Population was estimated at 49,309 on July 1, 2025. The median owned home is worth $472,500, and 77.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $1,644 and household income $133,037, so buyers here are well funded and picky about condition.

One resident in four is past 65, so many Chesterfield sellers are downsizing or settling an estate rather than relocating for work. Monthly owner costs run $2,464 with a mortgage and $946 without one, which tells you what a buyer will weigh against your asking price.

Parts of the city sit in the Missouri River floodplain, a valley once called Gumbo Flats. Ask your lender or title company whether your parcel needs flood insurance.

Two districts serve the city. Rockwood School District covers the western part and Parkway School District covers the east, and schools inside the city include Parkway Central, Parkway West and Marquette high schools. Buyers often ask the district first, so put it in your notes.

Repairs and additions go through the city's Planning Department. A building permit confirms that a project is structurally sound and meets building and zoning codes. Call the department before work on structure, additions or exterior changes.

The city's occupancy permit requirement is written for businesses: a permit or re-occupancy permit applies to every new business and every change of business use, tenancy or ownership. If you own a commercial space or a mixed property, that rule matters to your buyer. For an ordinary house sale, ask Chesterfield's Planning Department whether any permit applies to your address.

Occupancy approvals check compliance with city, county and fire district codes, so expect more than one office to be involved. Close any open permit before you list.

The St. Louis County Assessor values every parcel, and state law section 137.115 requires reassessment as of January 1 of each odd-numbered year. The assessor does not run the appeals board, which is independent. Appeals must be filed or postmarked by the second Monday in July.

The Collector of Revenue bills property tax, and it must be paid or postmarked by December 31 of the billed year. Payments made after that date are subject to up to 18 percent annual interest plus a 2 percent penalty under Missouri law.

Property tax is a lien on the house, so expect the closing agent to confirm the current year. Ask the collector's office for the exact balance on your parcel.

Deeds for Chesterfield are recorded with the St. Louis County Recorder of Deeds, 41 S. Central Avenue, Clayton, MO 63105. You can mail or drop off the original notarized document with a check or money order made out to ROD, or use an approved eRecording vendor. The original comes back within about a week of recording. Most owners leave this step to the title company.

The Missouri River valley flooded badly in 1993, and levees were raised afterward. The valley is now commercial, with Spirit of St. Louis Airport and a long strip of stores, but a house near the floodplain can still raise questions at closing. Your lender will tell you whether flood insurance is required, and a buyer's lender will ask the same thing. If you carry a policy, keep a copy of the declarations page for the buyer, since a transferable policy can be a selling point.

The soil in the valley turns to mud when wet, which is where the old Gumbo Flats name came from. Walk the lot after a heavy rain and note any pooling or foundation moisture, then fix drainage or disclose it before the buyer's inspector finds it.

sections.h2: Documents to gather before you list
sections.html:
A seller who has the paperwork ready can answer a buyer in a day instead of a week. Collect these first:

  • Your mortgage payoff letter from the lender.
  • The St. Louis County tax statement and proof that earlier years are paid.
  • Permit history, including any open or unclosed permit from past work.
  • The school district for the address, either Rockwood or Parkway.
  • A copy of your recorded deed from the Recorder of Deeds in Clayton.

Ask the title company to run a search early. A lien, an old release that was never recorded or a permit left open can delay a closing by weeks, and each is easier to fix before a contract is signed than after. Missouri tax is a lien on the house, so the title company will confirm the year's balance before closing and divide it between you and the buyer.

Because values are high and buyers are choosy, a Chesterfield house in good condition can attract the open market and sell on an agent's listing. A house that needs a kitchen, roof or systems work, or one tied up in an estate, may do better with a direct as-is purchase where the buyer handles repairs.

Get your payoff letter, county tax statement, school district and any permit history together first. With those in hand, you can compare an agent's net proceeds with a cash offer on equal terms.

If you are settling an estate, ask the title company early what court or probate papers they need before they will close, and whether anyone else holds an interest in the house. Cash buyers can often close in a few weeks, since there is no lender, but the county tax statement and deed recording steps stay the same. When you compare offers, count the closing costs, any repairs a listing buyer would request and the months of carrying costs while the house sits.

faqs.q: Which county records a Chesterfield deed?
faqs.a: St. Louis County, through the Recorder of Deeds at 41 S. Central Avenue in Clayton. A deed costs $26 for the first page and $3 for each extra page.

faqs.q: When are St. Louis County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31 of the billed year, with the postmark counting for mailed payments. Later payments accrue up to 18 percent yearly interest plus a 2 percent penalty.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my St. Louis County value?
faqs.a: Appeals are filed with the independent Board of Equalization, due by the second Monday in July. Ask the board when the next window opens.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Chesterfield house in?
faqs.a: Rockwood School District serves the west side of the city and Parkway School District serves the east. Confirm the district for your address with the school district's boundary tools before listing.

faqs.q: Does Chesterfield's occupancy permit apply when I sell my home?
faqs.a: The occupancy permit requirement is aimed at businesses, covering new businesses and changes of use, tenancy or ownership. Call the Planning Department to confirm for your address.
